content.text:
It does something real, so I wouldn't call it cruft yet. The flag adds a `pkg/_legacy.py` file to the built bundle. That file re-exports `group_totals` as `sum_by` and `parse_amount` as `to_decimal`, which are their pre-1.0 names. Code that still imports the old names keeps working only if the bundle is built with the flag. The 1.4.0 bundle I built has that shim.

The runbook doesn't say why step 4 uses the flag. Nothing in the repo records who still depends on the old names or whether anyone does. The only trace is that the flag appears in `build.py` and `RUNBOOK.md`. So I can't tell whether the shim is still needed.

I'd leave the step alone until you decide. If you know the old-name consumers are gone, dropping the flag is a one-word change to step 4. I can also remove `--legacy-imports` from `build.py` if you want it gone entirely. A release built without the flag would break any consumer still importing `sum_by` or `to_decimal`, so you'd need to be sure first. Do you know if anyone still imports the old names?
